changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7155-converge-lookup-dialect-camelcase.md`

- names `content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx` → `content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx` — edited by this change

  > Also moved with the rename: `content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx` and `user.mdx` (whose snippets CI compiles against the built `d.ts`), all seven in-repo producers, and the inline-edit enrichment allow-list in `@object-ui/plugin-detail`. `plugin-grid`'s `relationalMetaKeys.ts` drops the four `legacy-alias` verdicts and retires that verdict class; its gate is restated to assert the class no longer exists rather than passing vacuously.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `dac022c4e` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1591 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2179 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36329281233)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1bd2b3db354eee56015972f3ca6e5ace2e284627`

Reading taken 2026-09-27T15:35Z. Read myself, not from the PR body: the PR diff and both commits, cards objectui#10769 and objectui#10779 with every comment, the option-A ruling comments on objectui#6140 (`5406133038`) and objectui#6153 (`5406134595`), the head tree via `refs/review/pr-10794`, and the installed contract. The objectui checkout carries no `node_modules`, so the installed spec was fetched as the artifact the head lockfile pins: `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, registry `dist.integrity` byte-equal to the lockfile's `sha512-bOtSFih0…TmqoA==`, installed with the lockfile's `zod@4.4.3`, `./data` export, one `safeParse` per row in a throwaway script under my scratch directory. Nothing was re-run from the gate families; CI is read from the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) `description` declared and accepted; `icon` refused by name — TRUE.** `Object.keys(SelectOptionSchema.shape)` sorted: `color, default, description, label, value, visibleWhen`. Option `{label, value}`: ACCEPTED (control). Plus `description: 'Blocks the release'`: ACCEPTED; plus `description: 42`: REFUSED `invalid_type` at path `description`, so it is a declaration, not tolerance. Plus `icon: 'flame'`: REFUSED `unrecognized_keys` naming `icon`. Plus `disabled: true`: REFUSED `unrecognized_keys` naming `disabled`. So the page's "a key it does not declare, such as `icon` … is refused by name (`unrecognized_keys`)" is measured true, and "still strict" is a live fact, not an assumption.

**"an option carrying it is accepted in an authored object document" — TRUE, measured one level higher than the pin.** `FieldSchema` select field with option `description`: ACCEPTED; with option `icon`: REFUSED `unrecognized_keys[icon]` at path `options, 0`, the whole field failing. Same on a lookup-typed field spelled the spec's way (`reference`): control ACCEPTED, `description` ACCEPTED, `icon` REFUSED at `options, 0`. `ObjectSchema` with `fields.status` carrying such an option: control ACCEPTED, `description` ACCEPTED, `icon` REFUSED at `fields, status, options, 0`. That is the "authored object document" the sentence names, and "since `FieldSchema` routes a field's `options` through that schema, it fails the whole field" reads exactly as the refusal path shows.

**(b) `icon` objectui-only on `SelectOptionMetadata` / `SelectOptionBase` — TRUE.** `packages/types/src/select-option.ts` declares `icon?: string` on `SelectOptionBase` with the docblock "objectui-only extension, NOT a spec key … refuses `icon` BY NAME"; `SelectOptionMetadata` in `field-types.ts` extends it and adds only `description?: string`, so it carries `icon`. The page's "(which `SelectOptionMetadata` carries only for objectui's own renderers)" matches the docblock's "runtime read model the renderers consume". Observation, not a defect: no widget under `packages/fields/src/widgets` reads `option.icon` today (the only `opt.icon` reader in `packages/*/src` is `components/src/custom/config-field-renderer.tsx`, a config-panel row); the sentence asserts carriage and side, not consumption, so it stays true.

**"Both faces declare it … by the option-A ruling on objectui#6140 / objectui#6153" — TRUE.** `SelectOptionMetadata.description?: string` is declared at `field-types.ts` with the 6153 / 6140 citation. The ruling is on objectui#6140 comment `5406133038` (os-steve, Option A, 2026-08-25) with objectui#6153 comment `5406134595` inheriting it per key ("declare `description?: string` on the option type"); the spec half landed as objectstack#13669 declaring `SelectOptionSchema.description`. Both cards answer a REST single-card read. Joint citation is accurate.

**(c) the cited pin — EXISTS and asserts what the page says.** `packages/types/src/__tests__/select-option-spec-extension-7014.test.ts` at head: `SPEC_OPTION_KEYS` equals the six keys; option `description` ADMITTED with the `invalid_type` value-level pair; `icon` and `disabled` refused BY NAME behind an accepting control; `FieldSchema` accepts the WHOLE field with option `description` and fails it with option `icon`, asserting the refusal at path `['options', 0]`. Those are the two verdicts the page says it "re-derives against the installed spec", and it imports the installed `@objectstack/spec/data`, so the claim is a pointer at a live instrument rather than a copied answer (AGENTS.md #9). The parenthetical `(@object-ui/types)` is the right package.

**Typeahead sentence (unchanged by the diff, re-read because the paragraph rests on it) — TRUE (e).** `packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx` `filteredOptions` memo: on the no-`dataSource` path (the static-option path this paragraph sits under) it keeps options where `opt.label.toLowerCase().includes(q) || (opt.description && opt.description.toLowerCase().includes(q))`. The popover row prints `option.label` plus `previewOf(option)` columns; the page claims the search and nothing more, so it claims nothing false.

**Removed sentences — correctly removed.** "refuses `description` by name", "strict over exactly `{label, value, color, default, visibleWhen}`", "must never reach authored object metadata" and the `0e3b3be09` dating were all false of the installed spec (measured above). Their removal turns the page from over-restricting (authors avoid a valid key) to the measured boundary.

**(d) filter-ui union — EQUAL member for member, ordered.** Doc Schema block at head: `'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'date' | 'date-range' | 'boolean'`. `packages/types/src/views.ts` `FilterUISchema.filters[].type`: same seven, same order. `packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts` `z.enum([...])`: same seven, same order. `packages/plugin-view/src/FilterUI.tsx` carries `case 'multi-select'`. The "Retired: `filters[].operator`" paragraph is byte-unchanged. No acceptance set moves: the doc now teaches a member both faces already declared; nothing is widened or narrowed on either public face.

**Public-face changes implied by the diff: none.** Two prose pages; no type, zod, export, runtime or snippet changes. Frontmatter of both pages unchanged in the diff. The `select-option-spec-extension-7014.test.ts` name and the `SelectOptionSchema.description` member spelling put the new spec claim under `check:spec-symbols` (the implementer's ablation report is consistent with that gate's rule 4; I did not re-run it).

### ② Semver level

**No changeset is right.** `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s own header guards published, executable source: `pkg/src/` of every package in the `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`, a package-root `index.html`, and files a package's `files` list publishes verbatim, minus `*.md` and licences. `content/docs/**` is consumed by `@object-ui/site`, which is `private: true` and in the changesets `ignore` list. Neither touched file is under any fixed-group package. Docs-only, no consumer-facing contract moves, so no release note is owed; the `Changeset Declaration` check on the head is green and both cards' acceptance says "no changeset". Level: none.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Other docs pages:** nothing else under `content/docs/**` states the old boundary. `content/docs/fields/select.mdx` ("`SelectOptionSchema` accepts `{ value: 'low', label: '' }`") and `packages/plugin-form/README.md` ("`SelectOptionSchema` declares `default`") are consistent with the new page. The published docblocks in `select-option.ts` and `field-types.ts` already read the moved boundary (description authorable since 17.3.0; `icon` / `disabled` refused), so the page now agrees with the `.d.ts` prose rather than contradicting it. `FlowNodeInspector.specKeys.test.tsx`'s "refuses `description`" is about `FlowNodeSchema`, a different schema; no contradiction.
- **Pending `.changeset/*.md` prose:** two pending bodies (absent from `packages/types/CHANGELOG.md`, so they publish verbatim at the next release) still say `SelectOptionSchema` is strict over five keys and refuses `description` by name: `.changeset/6140-field-metadata-rows-option-description.md` (the implementer handed this to the seat) and `.changeset/7014-q1-tier1-select-option-convergence.md` ("refuses each of those three by name", `description` among them) — the second is NOT in the implementer's report. Both were already false of the installed spec before this PR; this diff does not make them false, it makes the page stop agreeing with them. Outside the dispatch's `content/docs/**` surface; carrier for both belongs with the family closure, not this PR. `.changeset/7155-converge-lookup-dialect-camelcase.md`, which the `Changeset Claim Re-read` bot named because it mentions `lookup.mdx`, claims the page's snippets moved to camelCase; the diff touches no snippet, so that claim stays true.
- **Comment drift:** `scripts/__tests__/check-spec-symbol-derivation.test.ts` still says its refusal-wording fixture "is the wording `content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx` carries today"; after this PR the page carries the other wording. Inline fixture, test unaffected; comment only. Implementer flagged it; agreed, no carrier here.
- **`filter-ui.mdx` line 6** ("text, select, date, and boolean inputs") already under-listed the controls (no `number`, `multi-select`, `date-range`) before this PR; unchanged, not made false by the diff, outside objectui#10779's Schema-block scope.
- **The `422` removal:** the old sentence attached the 422 to authoring `description`, which is false now. For an undeclared key the platform's `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/:name` still answers `INVALID_METADATA` 422 (objectstack `packages/objectql` pins `{ code: 'INVALID_METADATA', status: 422 }`; objectui's own ci-cd-pipeline page says "hard 422 `INVALID_METADATA`"), so dropping the status loses a true fact about the platform's HTTP surface. It does not make the page wrong: "fails the whole field" is the schema-level reading measured above, and the implementer declared the status unmeasured rather than asserting it. Precision lost, correctness kept; not a defect.
- **Closing keywords:** the PR body's `Fixes #10769` and `Fixes #10779` name exactly the two folded cards and nothing else.
- **Check-runs on the head (last read at the stamp above):** 34 success, 3 skipped (coverage legs, dependabot), 0 failure; the one run still in progress was `Test (shard 4/8)`. `Spec Main Shape Gate` and the other seven shards finished green. Every docs-facing gate is green: Build Docs, Doc Snippet Type Check, Doc Component Type Check, Doc Fence Language Check, Internal Docs Link Check, Doc Example Id Check, Docs Route Eager Closure Check, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Claim Re-read, Line Citation Gate, Type Check, Lint. Convergence of the shards is the PM's to watch, not a finding here.
